title: Future -bo and continuous -chi
focus: Future (ami jabo, tumi jabe, o jabe) and present continuous (ami khacchi, tumi korcho); plans and what's happening now.
body:
# Future -bo and continuous -chi

Two new tenses this time: the **future** (*I will eat*) and the **present continuous** (*I am eating right now*). Both work like the simple past: take the stem and add an ending for the person.

**Future:** ami → **-bo**, tumi → **-be**, o → **-be**. So **ami jabo** (I'll go), **tumi jabe** (you'll go), **o jabe** (he/she'll go). Use it for plans, offers and promises, often with **kal** (tomorrow).

**Continuous:** ami → **-chi**, tumi → **-cho**, o → **-che**. So **ami korchi** (I'm doing), **tumi korcho** (you're doing), **o korche** (he/she's doing). When the stem ends in a vowel (kha-, ja-, de-), the ch doubles: **khacchi**, **jacchi**, **dicchi**.

| Verb | Future: ami / tumi, o | Continuous: ami / tumi / o |
|---|---|---|
| khaoa (eat) | khabo / khabe | khacchi / khaccho / khacche |
| jaoa (go) | jabo / jabe | jacchi / jaccho / jacche |
| kora (do) | korbo / korbe | korchi / korcho / korche |
| asha (come) | ashbo / ashbe | ashchi / ashcho / ashche |
| deoa (give) | debo / debe | dicchi / diccho / dicche |
| kena (buy) | **kinbo** / kinbe | **kinchi** / kincho / kinche |
| ghumono (sleep) | ghumobo / ghumobe | ghumocchi / ghumoccho / ghumocche |

**kena** uses the same **kin-** stem you met in the past (kinlam). For "we" (amra) use the ami forms, and for "they" (ora) use the o forms.

## Examples

- **tumi cha khabe?**: will you have some tea? (the normal way to offer)
- **ami kal korbo**: I'll do it tomorrow
- **o kal jabe**: he/she will go tomorrow
- **ami tomake debo**: I'll give it to you
- **kal dekha hobe**: see you tomorrow
- **tumi ki korcho?**: what are you doing?
- **Ollie ghumocche**: Ollie is sleeping
- **ami ashchi!**: I'm coming!
- **brishti hocche**: it's raining
- **Ollie ekhon khacche, ami pore khabo**: Ollie is eating now, I'll eat later

## Common mistakes

- ❌ **ami kheyechi** for "I'm eating". That means *I've eaten*. Right now is ✅ **ami khacchi**.
- ❌ **tumi khabo**. The -bo ending is only for ami. With tumi and o, use ✅ **tumi khabe**, ✅ **o khabe**.

same -be ending as tumi; only ami gets -bo
jaoa → ja- + -be; the future uses the plain stem ja-, not ge-
kal + future = tomorrow; kal + past = yesterday
lit. 'you tea will-eat?'; the everyday way to offer tea
ki (what) goes right before the verb
kothay (where) + jabe (you will go)
kora → kor- + -bo; 'it' is left out
kena → kin- + -bo; same kin- stem as kinlam
tomake = to you; deoa → de- + -bo
lit. 'tomorrow seeing will happen'; hobe = will happen
ja- + -cchi; the ch doubles after a vowel stem
kor- + -cho (the tumi continuous ending)
kha- + -ccho; compare tumi khao = you eat (in general)
ghumono → ghumo- + -cche (the o ending)
asha → ash- + -chi; also said when you're about to leave: 'I'm off'
pora → por- + -chi; no 'a' needed before boi
lit. 'rain is happening'; hoa → ho- + -cche
ja- + -ccho; compare kothay jabe? = where will you go?
tomake = you (object); dekh- + -chi
